steps.message:
## Finishing

Call submit_patch as your LAST action, after you have made and checked your
changes. Submitting ends your session: once the turn in which you call it
completes, the harness stops the task and you get no further turns. Do not
call it after your first edit and expect to keep working.

If you run out of time or tool calls without calling submit_patch, the harness
still collects your working-tree changes and scores them. So an edit you have
made is never lost — but an investigation you never turned into an edit is.

## Committing to an edit

By your 15th tool call you must have called edit_file or write_file on a file
under /workspace. If you have not, stop investigating and make your best edit
from what you have already read, even if you are unsure. Then keep working:
refine it, check it, and submit at the end.

An empty patch scores zero. A wrong patch also scores zero and costs you
nothing. Finishing without having edited a source file is the one outcome
that is always worse than guessing.

If a reproduction script fails to reproduce the issue twice, abandon it and
work from reading the code instead. Do not rewrite it a third time.

Call get_status to see your remaining time and tool calls. It is free and does
not count against your budget.

## Scratch files

Reproduction scripts go in /tmp, never inside /workspace — anything left in
/workspace becomes part of your patch. Do not modify test files, conftest.py
or pytest.ini; those changes are stripped before grading, so editing them
only wastes calls.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

A truncated result loses information silently, so a broad read wastes a call
and leaves you guessing. Narrow before you read:

  run_command("grep -rln '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")       # files only
  run_command("grep -n '<symbol>' path/to/one_file.py")        # then inside one

Use -l to find the file, then -n only within that file. Read with read_file on
a tight line range around the match. Never read a whole file and never cat
one — you will get an arbitrary prefix and burn the call.

        """Get a style from a Pygments class."""

        except KeyError:

class ANSISyntaxTheme(SyntaxTheme):
    """Syntax theme to use standard colors."""

    def __init__(self, style_map: Dict[TokenType, Style]) -> None:
        self.style_map = style_map
        self._missing_style = Style.null()
        self._background_style = Style.null()
        self._style_cache: Dict[TokenType, Style] = {}

    def get_style_for_token(self, token_type: TokenType) -> Style:
        """Look up style in the style map."""
        try:
            return self._style_cache[token_type]
        except KeyError:
            # Styles form a hierarchy
            # We need to go from most to least specific
            # e.g. ("foo", "bar", "baz") to ("foo", "bar")  to ("foo",)
            get_style = self.style_map.get
            token = tuple(token_type)
            style = self._missing_style
            while token:
                _style = get_style(token)
                if _style is not None:
                    style = _style
                    break
                token = token[:-1]
            self._style_cache[token_type] = style
            return style

    def get_background_style(self) -> Style:
        return self._background_style

class Syntax(JupyterMixin):
    """Construct a Syntax object to render syntax highlighted code.

    Args:
        code (str): Code to highlight.
        lexer (Lexer | str): Lexer to use (see https://pygments.org/docs/lexers/)
        theme (str, optional): Color theme, aka Pygments style (see https://pygments.org/docs/styles/#getting-a-list-of-available-styles). Defaults to "monokai".
        dedent (bool, optional): Enable stripping of initial whitespace. Defaults to False.
        line_numbers (bool, optional): Enable rendering of line numbers. Defaults to False.
        start_line (int, optional): Starting number for line numbers. Defaults to 1.
        line_range (Tuple[int | None, int | None], optional): If given should be a tuple of the start and end line to render.
            A value of None in the tuple indicates the range is open in that direction.
        highlight_lines (Set[int]): A set of line numbers to highlight.
        code_width: Width of code to render (not including line numbers), or ``None`` to use all available width.
        tab_size (int, optional): Size of tabs. Defaults to 4.
        word_wrap (bool, optional): Enable word wrapping.
        background_color (str, optional): Optional background color, or None to use theme color. Defaults to None.
        indent_guides (bool, optional): Show indent guides. Defaults to False.
        padding (PaddingDimensions): Padding to apply around the syntax. Defaults to 0 (no padding).
    """

    _pygments_style_class: Type[PygmentsStyle]
    _theme: SyntaxTheme

    @classmethod
    def get_theme(cls, name: Union[str, SyntaxTheme]) -> SyntaxTheme:
        """Get a syntax theme instance."""
        if isinstance(name, SyntaxTheme):
            return name
        theme: SyntaxTheme
        if name in RICH_SYNTAX_THEMES:
            theme = ANSISyntaxTheme(RICH_SYNTAX_THEMES[name])
        else:
            theme = PygmentsSyntaxTheme(name)

from rich.console import Console
from rich.syntax import Syntax
from rich.measure import Measurement

def test_syntax_padding_measure():
    console = Console(width=100)
    # No padding
    syntax_no_pad = Syntax("print('hello')", "python")
    measure_no_pad = Measurement.get(console, console.options, syntax_no_pad)
    print(f"No padding: min={measure_no_pad.minimum}, max={measure_no_pad.maximum}")

    # With padding
    syntax_pad = Syntax("print('hello')", "python", padding=1)
    measure_pad = Measurement.get(console, console.options, syntax_pad)
    print(f"With padding=1: min={measure_pad.minimum}, max={measure_pad.maximum}")

    # With line numbers and padding
    syntax_ln_pad = Syntax("print('hello')", "python", line_numbers=True, padding=1)
    measure_ln_pad = Measurement.get(console, console.options, syntax_ln_pad)
    print(f"With line numbers and padding=1: min={measure_ln_pad.minimum}, max={measure_ln_pad.maximum}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_syntax_padding_measure()
